answer.why: As an insider I laugh at it immediately. 'Confirmed' and 'Substantive' are the exact words from a posting or appointment letter, once you pass probation and when you stop being 'acting'. It tells me the makers know the service, so I'd trust the details more. 'Minister Salary' is the obvious hook, and the ministerial pay benchmark is the one thing every outsider already knows. It reads like clickbait to me, and I'd expect cheap jokes and a lot of details done wrong.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, slightly cynical game about chasing the big pay cheque: climb the ranks, reach the benchmarked ministerial salary, and probably take some digs at the 'highest paid politicians in the world' debate. I'd expect a number-goes-up game with a bit of political commentary, and I'd worry it would be shallow or get the institutions wrong.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, in-joke career sim about the slow, bureaucratic rhythm of public service life: probation, appraisals, acting appointments, and waiting to be made substantive. I'd expect it to be understated and wry, with accurate process detail, and I'd feel it was made for people like me, though a general audience might not get the name at all.

best_moment.what: The salary committee made my Cabinet question item three and I submitted under my own name. It was the insider joke done properly, a question you ask in a meeting becoming an agenda item with your name on it.

worst_moment.what: The GE year, with STAND sliding 86, 80, 74, 68, 64. It felt like a slow number counting down, and walking every block for nine days did not seem to get me any answer on workload.

skip_year.why: Nothing in the middle was truly unplayable, but the stretch of Y9-13 and Y14-19 went by in blocks of promotions with little to hold onto. If I had to pick, I would skip those.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Nominated a quiet officer for PSLP (Y1-8)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: She became Deputy Secretary and put my name forward

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y25 answered the true third point publicly in the Correction Direction
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Y27 the third point was adopted quietly and I alone said so on record

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y28 asked Cabinet whether ministers should be paid on indicators they set
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Y31 the salary committee made it item three, and Y32 the formula moved one point with my submission uncredited

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y38 (the ending card) let the nominee decide without hearing from me
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card said that choice raised my ceiling to Deputy Prime Minister

answer.held_back_by: Nothing held me back, really. The file put no ceiling on me, and I got to PM at 59 with a clean file. If anything, the thing that cost me was the workload question never being fixed and STAND eroding.
answer.ending_fair_why: PM with integrity 100 and a boring file matches how I played, mostly sensible and occasionally principled. The 'boring file is a compliment' line was fair. The declassified ceiling reveals made it feel like the game was explaining my own life back to me.
answer.chase_next: I would chase the version where I stay a technocrat and never go into politics, a Permanent Secretary who lasts. I want to see whether the service track alone has a satisfying ending, since the party estimate and ceiling reveals suggest there is a separate path.
answer.play_again_why: One run was enough for now. I am curious about the other ending, but I want to come back to it fresh instead of immediately after a 34-year life.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.
tone_breaks.note: A bit pointed and arguably winks at the real benchmark debate. As an insider I would read it as a dig rather than neutral description, though it is aimed at the system and not a person.

tone_breaks.line: RETIRED AS Prime Minister AT AGE 59
tone_breaks.note: Mostly fine, but the notes show a Minister jump to DPM and PM with no visible succession mechanics. In reality the party's choice of PM is a much more visible process and I would have wanted more of it on screen.

answer.title_fit_why: What stayed with me was the quiet institutional stuff: appraisals, wording, who gets credited, who nominates whom. The pay was a result line. Confirmed & Substantive sounds like an appraisal outcome, which is what the game is actually about.

YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.

EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
